subject: subset and dplyr::filter give different results when some columns are un-named

messages.author: a9c5da7cbde2173d
messages.subject: subset and dplyr::filter give different results when some columns are un-named
parts:
Hi,

If you read in data and only give names to some columns, then subset and filter give different results.  For example, assume the following data in file test.csv

1,11,16,21
2,12,17,22
3,13,18,23
4,14,19,24
5,15,20,25

> t  <-  read.csv("test.csv", header=FALSE)
> colnames(t) <- c("ID", "X")
> t
  ID  X NA NA
1  1 11 16 21
2  2 12 17 22
3  3 13 18 23
4  4 14 19 24
5  5 15 20 25
> 
> subset(t, ID < 3)
  ID  X NA NA.1
1  1 11 16   21
2  2 12 17   22

> t %>% dplyr::filter(ID < 3)
  ID  X NA NA
1  1 11 16 16
2  2 12 17 17

filter() seems to make multiple copies of the first NA column it encounters.  Obviously it is unwise to name some columns and not others, but it would be safer to make filter() more idiot-proof like subset(). 

Best wishes,
Jim
